Put the exception in one thread

Commerce operations run across store records, fulfillment, inventory, support, campaigns, and finance. The most important work is often an exception: a split shipment, an unusual return, low stock, or a promotion whose inputs disagree.

Maia can gather the selected facts and prepare the decision in Slack. The responsible operator chooses the remedy and approves any customer message or store change.

Review an order exception

Provide the order number, current store export or connected record, support history, policy, and shipping details available to the team. Maia can build a timestamped timeline, identify the discrepancy, and list missing facts.

The output should distinguish ordered, fulfilled, shipped, delivered, returned, and refunded states. Operations or CX decides whether to replace, refund, reroute, wait, or escalate. Maia does not treat a customer request as proof of the store state.

Prepare a return review

Give Maia the return request, order record, approved policy, customer messages, and shared photos when relevant. It can compare the supplied facts with the policy and draft a response that asks for any missing information.

Authorized staff determine eligibility and approve the customer communication or refund. This workflow supports consistent review without making Maia a fraud system or an autonomous returns desk.

Surface stock exceptions

For a scheduled stock brief, define the inventory source, timestamp, thresholds, active promotions, and recipient channel. Maia can list products that newly crossed a threshold and explain which source placed them there.

The merchandiser decides whether to reorder, hide, substitute, or leave the item available. A stock snapshot is not a real-time availability guarantee, so the brief should make freshness easy to see.

Check promotion readiness

Combine the promotion brief, offer rules, current inventory, required creative, tracking plan, and launch checklist. Maia can prepare a readiness packet with missing assets, stock risks, owner gaps, and decisions due.

Marketing and commerce owners confirm offers, timing, inventory assumptions, and publication. Campaign analysis should use named sources and date ranges rather than claim independent knowledge of revenue attribution.

Start with one order

Choose one order with a missing shipping update and a return question. Ask Maia for the timeline, policy references, and a proposed customer reply. The operator can resolve the missing fact, edit the response, and decide the next action from the same thread.

Once the team resolves the order, Maia can prepare the internal recap and customer draft from the same decision. The recap records what staff confirmed, what action they chose, and which follow-up remains. That gives the next shift a clear history if the customer returns.

Questions from commerce teams

Which store systems can Maia use?

Confirm the exact commerce connection and reads in your setup. Authorized exports can support the first exception review.

Can Maia issue refunds or cancel orders?

Only a supported action with the right authority should propose that change. An operator reviews the exact order, amount, reason, and message first.

Can Maia monitor inventory in real time?

Maia can prepare reports from the source and refresh schedule you provide. Always show the timestamp and avoid presenting a snapshot as live availability.
